mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth, as indicated by GDPC1, suggests a robust economy, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in most 60-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) may lead to wage inflation, prompting tighter monetary policy and potentially negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE remains low but S&P 500 returns are positive in most 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, which may boost corporate revenues and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises but S&P 500 returns are negative in most 60-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high, the Fed may tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 is strong and CPIAUCSL is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in most 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS) may lead to higher wages and inflation, prompting Fed rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are positive in most 20-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST and RSAFS are strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in most 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% may indicate tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in most 5-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.
